updates.finding: A senior Iranian official told Reuters Iran would make no nuclear concessions even if the United States accepted Tehran's Hormuz proposal and said the waterway would remain closed until all Iranian conditions were met. The statement separated the Hormuz package from Iran's nuclear red lines.
updates.status: IRANIAN NO-FLEXIBILITY NUCLEAR POSITION REPORTED; ANONYMOUS SENIOR-OFFICIAL SOURCE; NO AGREEMENT
updates.drawer_effect: UPDATE U.S.-Iran negotiation drawer by separating Hormuz/war-ending conditions from Iran's stated nuclear position; retain anonymous-source provenance.

updates.finding: Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Iran had given the United States a concrete seven-day plan under which the Strait of Hormuz could reopen and normal maritime passage could resume if U.S. actions already contemplated in the June MOU were taken. He placed the next move on Washington.
updates.status: SEVEN-DAY IRANIAN PROPOSAL PUBLICLY CONFIRMED BY FOREIGN MINISTER; U.S. ACCEPTANCE NOT ESTABLISHED AT STATEMENT TIME
updates.drawer_effect: SUPERSEDE the generic phased-framework description with the publicly stated Iranian seven-day proposal while preserving that this remained a proposal, not an agreement.

updates.update_type: diplomacy / U.S. response to Iranian proposal
updates.finding: Reuters reported President Trump said he had rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end regional fighting. Earlier reporting had cited the Wall Street Journal saying Trump privately rejected the proposal and considered renewed bombing likely after U.S. midterms; the direct public rejection superseded the earlier anonymous-source report as the stronger response record.
updates.status: U.S. PRESIDENTIAL REJECTION PUBLICLY STATED; IRANIAN SEVEN-DAY PROPOSAL NOT ACCEPTED
updates.drawer_effect: UPDATE U.S.-Iran negotiation outcome from pending response to public U.S. presidential rejection. Keep claims about future bombing plans separate unless independently confirmed.

updates.finding: The military chiefs of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey met in Riyadh and, according to Pakistan's military, discussed intelligence sharing, military coordination, capability integration and threats facing Saudi Arabia. The meeting turned the earlier planned consultation into an observed alliance-implementation step, while specific deployments or operational commitments were not established.
updates.status: MILITARY-CHIEFS MEETING CONFIRMED; COORDINATION AREAS ANNOUNCED; SPECIFIC DEPLOYMENTS/COMBAT COMMITMENTS NOT ESTABLISHED
updates.drawer_effect: UPDATE Makkah pact from planned crisis consultation to completed chiefs-level coordination meeting; do not infer troop deployment or combat participation.

updates.finding: Reuters reported oil prices fell about 3% on Friday as hopes for a U.S.-Iran truce increased, while traders simultaneously priced supply risk from Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. The move reflected market expectations rather than proof of a diplomatic settlement.
updates.status: MARKET PRICED SOME TRUCE OPTIMISM; HOUTHI SUPPLY RISK REMAINED; NO SETTLEMENT IMPLIED
updates.drawer_effect: UPDATE market-sentiment drawer; preserve market pricing as expectation rather than evidence of agreement.
